history.action: route plan -> implement -> review -> qa (model, confidence 88)

validated_work_order.understanding: A category filter value like `%%%%%%Z` typed into a Custom report freezes the browser's main thread for minutes on a budget with several hundred categories. CustomReport.tsx:204 marks a `category` + `contains/doesNotContain/matches/hasTags` condition as `isComplexCategoryCondition`, which routes the report through `createCustomSpreadsheet` (custom-spreadsheet.ts:93) and `createGroupedSpreadsheet` (grouped-spreadsheet.ts:45), whose bodies call `narrowCategoriesByConditions` -> `filterCategoriesByConditions` -> `likePatternToRegex('%' + value + '%')` once per category per condition, every render. Each unescaped `%` compiles to `.*` and `.test()` backtracks over the partitions of the category name. I re-measured the cost on this runner (300 categories, names ~30 chars): 4 wildcards 46 ms, 5 -> 375 ms, 6 -> 2.5 s, 7 -> 15.6 s - roughly 8x per added wildcard, with compile time <=0.09 ms in every row. The cost is in `.test()`, not compilation, so memoisation cannot be the fix. `unicodeLike` (the sqlite `UNICODE_LIKE` scalar) goes through the same function and already memoises through an LRU, so it needs neither a second bound nor its own cache. The bound belongs in `likePatternToRegex` and must be expressible in its return type, because a caller that cannot see a refusal will silently compile the catastrophic regex. It must fail OPEN: a refusal keeps every category, on both operators - including `doesNotContain`, which is the trap, because a refusal represented as a match-everything regex negates to 'drop everything' and drops every category the query fetched.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Unbounded wildcard expansion in the LIKE-pattern compiler. `likePatternToRegex` (packages/loot-core/src/shared/likePattern.ts:16) translates every unescaped `%` into `.*` with no limit (line 30-31), and the regex engine backtracks over the partitions of the subject string on `.test()`. The report axis runs that `.test()` once per category per condition on every render, so a value with six `%` is an 8-wildcard pattern against every category name. The cost is in matching, not compiling: compilation was <=0.09 ms for every pattern I measured, including the one that takes 15.6 s to test, so caching the regex (which `unicodeLike` already does) cannot fix it.
validated_work_order.approach:
Make `likePatternToRegex` return `RegExp | null`, refusing a pattern that is over-long or over-wildcarded, and teach its two consumers to treat `null` as 'matches every string' so the failure direction is open everywhere.

1. The bound, in `likePattern.ts` only: two module-private constants - `MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH = 256` (the same number and precedent as the `matches` guard at budgetDataQuery.ts:274-278) and `MAX_UNESCAPED_WILDCARDS = 4`. Count only unescaped `%` and unescaped `?`; a `\\%` compiles to a literal and adds no `.*`. Return `null` before `new RegExp(...)` is ever constructed. The wildcard count, not the length, is what carries AC-1: six `%` is an 8-character pattern no length cap would catch.

2. Why 4, measured on this runner (300 categories, ~30-char names, value = `%`x n + 'Z', run before writing this order): 4 wildcards 46 ms total, 5 -> 375 ms, 6 -> 2465 ms, 7 -> 15555 ms; compile <=0.09 ms in every row, ~8x per added wildcard. A cap of 4 keeps the accepted region at tens of milliseconds across 300 categories and cuts everything from 375 ms upward. It also preserves today's pinned behaviour: `contains '%'` and `contains '?'` compile to 3-wildcard patterns (`%%%` and `%?%`) and still match everything - verified by running the compiler on both.

3. Why `RegExp | null` and not a match-everything regex. THE TRAP: `contains` keeps a category when the regex matches, `doesNotContain` keeps it when it does NOT. Returning `/^[\s\S]*$/i` therefore fails OPEN for `contains` and fails CLOSED for `doesNotContain` - it drops every category, the money-losing direction AC-3 exists to prevent. `null` forces each call site to decide explicitly and TypeScript refuses to let a future consumer forget.

THE RULE: a refused pattern is treated as matching every string, and every consumer of a refusal KEEPS every category - including the `doesNotContain` branch, which returns `true` on a refusal rather than negating a match-everything result.

WORKED EXAMPLES (computed, value `%%%%%%Z`, 8 wildcards, refused): `contains` -> axis keeps all N categories; query `$like` -> `UNICODE_LIKE` returns 1 for every row -> every transaction returned; axis == result set, totals unchanged, real balances. `doesNotContain` -> axis keeps all N categories (NOT zero); query `$notlike` -> `NOT 1` -> no transactions; axis strictly WIDER than the result set, every kept category at 0.00.

INVARIANT: for any refused pattern and any budget, the categories the axis renders are a SUPERSET of those in the query's result set - no category the query fetched loses its row, no money leaves a total because a value was too long. Every refusal path returns 'keep', so the bound cannot violate it.

THE ONE PLACE THE REFUSAL PATH IS NOT IDENTITY - stated here because the last review caught the plan claiming otherwise, and the claim was wrong. `narrowCategoriesByConditions` short-circuits on `list === categories.list` (line 151) to skip rebuilding the grouped array. `filterCategoriesByConditions` returns its input untouched only on the three early returns at lines 176, 192 and 202 (no conditions, no category conditions, uninterpretable condition). On the refusal path it reaches line 291, `return categories.filter(cat => ...)`, and `Array.prototype.filter` always allocates. So `list === categories.list` is false, the identity shortcut does not fire, and the function falls through to the rebuild at lines 155-167. THIS PLAN THEREFORE ASSERTS CONTENTS, NOT IDENTITY. For a refused pattern the function returns a NEW object whose `list` is a new array holding the same category entities in the same order, and whose `grouped` is a new array of new group objects each still holding all of its members - with one further consequence the tests must pin: line 166 ends in `.filter(group => group.categories.length > 0)`, so a group that was ALREADY EMPTY in the input is dropped, exactly as it is for any narrowing filter today (`contains '%'` takes this same rebuild path on unmodified main, so this is not a regression). A dropped empty group holds no categories, so no money moves with it - it costs an empty row at most, which is the safe direction. No change is made to make the refusal path return by identity; see alternatives_considered.

HOW THAT LOOKS ON SCREEN: a `doesNotContain` filter holding a refused value gives every category a balance of 0.00, so the screen depends on `showEmpty`, which defaults to false (ReportOptions.ts:25). With showEmpty false, `filterEmptyRows` (filterEmptyRows.ts:24) drops every zero-balance row and the report renders an empty table - identical for a correct and a fail-closed build, so it is not a usable assertion. With showEmpty true, every category survives at 0.00; a fail-closed build narrows the axis to nothing and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:56 takes `categoryList.length === 0` and calls `setData([])`. AC-3 therefore runs with 'Show empty rows' enabled.

files.change: Add two module-private constants - `MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH = 256` and `MAX_UNESCAPED_WILDCARDS = 4`, both unexported - and change the signature to `export function likePatternToRegex(pattern: string): RegExp | null`. Return `null` when `pattern.length > MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH` before compiling anything. Inside the existing while loop keep a `wildcards` counter incremented only on the unescaped `%` branch (line 30) and the unescaped `?` branch (line 32) - NOT on the escaped-wildcard branch at lines 21-28, where `\\%` compiles to a literal - and return `null` when the count exceeds `MAX_UNESCAPED_WILDCARDS`, before `new RegExp(regexStr, 'i')` at line 39 is ever constructed. Extend the module doc comment with the contract every consumer now depends on: 'returns null for a pattern it refuses; a refused pattern is to be treated as matching every string, and the caller must then keep everything rather than drop it'. Add the measured curve (4/5/6/7 wildcards -> 46 ms / 375 ms / 2465 ms / 15555 ms across 300 categories, compile <=0.09 ms throughout) and say in one line why the bound is the fix and not memoisation. Delete the trailing `// ? added here` on line 25; keep `// escaped wildcard - treat as literal character` above it. Drop `export` from `REGEX_SPECIAL` (line 14), keeping both in-module uses on lines 25 and 35.
files.why: The file the ticket says the bound is defined in, and the only place both consumers inherit it. The `null` return makes a refusal visible to a caller instead of silently compiling the catastrophic regex.

files.change: Retype the LRU to `new LRUCache<string, RegExp | null>({ max: 500 })`. Replace the `if (!cachedRegExp)` block at lines 14-18 with an `=== undefined` sentinel (`let cached = likePatternCache.get(pattern); if (cached === undefined) { cached = likePatternToRegex(pattern); likePatternCache.set(pattern, cached); }`) - a cached `null` is falsy, so the existing check would recompile per row instead of caching the refusal. After the lookup, `if (cached === null) return 1;` with a comment stating why a refusal returns a MATCH: under `$like` that returns every transaction (equal to the axis, which also keeps everything) and under `$notlike` none (a strict subset of the axis), so in both directions the axis is never narrower than the result set. Add no second bound and no second memoisation. The `if (!pattern) return 0` early return at line 11 is untouched.
files.why: AC-2 requires the sqlite UNICODE_LIKE path to inherit the bound rather than grow a second check, so this consumer handles `null` and nothing more.

files.change: Four edits. (1) `contains` branch (line 246): hoist `const pattern = getNormalisedString('%' + condition.value + '%')` and `const matcher = likePatternToRegex(pattern)`, keep the `typeof condition.value === 'string' &&` guard (line 248) so today's exact semantics are preserved, and return `matcher === null || matcher.test(getNormalisedString(textValue))`. (2) `doesNotContain` branch (line 258): the same hoist with the same string guard, and return `matcher === null ? true : !matcher.test(getNormalisedString(textValue))` - a refusal must return `true` and KEEP the category, with a comment naming the trap: negating a match-everything result would drop every category, the money-losing direction. Keep the existing comments on why the axis runs the query's two primitives; `isSupportedCategoryCondition` already guarantees a string value, so the new guards are defensive only. (3) Drop `export` from `canNarrowAxisByConditions` (line 89; sole caller is line 137 of the same file, imported by no test - verified by grep) and record in its doc comment that it is unexported rather than given a direct test because all four branches are already covered through its only observable contract, `narrowCategoriesByConditions`'s. (4) CORRECT TWO COMMENTS THAT THIS CHANGE MAKES WRONG, per .sdlc/memory/conventions.md ('comments describe the current state'): the doc comment at lines 115-125 says 'When no condition narrows anything, the input is returned unchanged by identity' - after this change a refused pattern narrows nothing yet does NOT return by identity, so reword it to name the three cases that do (no conditions, no category conditions, an uninterpretable condition) and say that every other path goes through `Array.prototype.filter` and rebuilds. The comment at lines 148-150 says '`filterCategoriesByConditions` returns its input untouched whenever it cannot safely narrow' - narrow 'whenever' to 'when it cannot interpret the conditions', and add that a refused pattern is also a keep-everything result but reaches the `.filter()` at line 291 and therefore rebuilds. `matches` at lines 274-284 is untouched.
files.why: The axis is the money path. Both LIKE call sites must decide the refusal explicitly, and `doesNotContain` is the one that decides it the wrong way by default. Edit (4) exists because a comment that misdescribes the code it sits above is a defect this repo has been merged for repeatedly (see .sdlc/memory/patterns/planner-read-comment-wording-as-the-defect.md).

cases: Add a module-level helper `matches(pattern, value)` that calls `likePatternToRegex`, throws if it returns null, and returns `.test(value)` - then route the ~15 existing assertions (lines 7-57) through it. Required by the type change, and it doubles as the AC-4 regression suite: every existing case (`%%%` matching every string, `\\%` as a literal, `_` NOT a wildcard, case-insensitivity) now also proves the bound refuses nothing plausible. No non-null assertion.

New describe block 'bounds the pattern': `likePatternToRegex('%' + '%%%%%%' + 'Z' + '%')` is null (8 unescaped wildcards) and `likePatternToRegex('%' + '%%%%%' + '%')` is null - the exact value AC-1 names, wrapped the way the `contains` branch wraps it.
Boundary from both sides: the 4-wildcard pattern `'%' + '%%Z' + '%'` is NOT null and still matches, so the cap is 4 and not 3.
The count is over UNESCAPED wildcards only: `'\\%'.repeat(20)` is not refused, because it compiles to literals and adds no `.*`.

Length cap independently: `'x'.repeat(257)` is null, `'x'.repeat(256)` is not, matching the existing 256-character guard at budgetDataQuery.ts:274-278. Note in a comment that `contains` wraps the value in two more `%`, so a 256-char VALUE becomes a 258-char pattern and is length-refused while a 254-char value is not - the length cap is a safety net, and the wildcard count is what carries AC-1.
A refused pattern is refused structurally rather than by cost - the return is null, not a RegExp. Do NOT write a wall-clock timing assertion; it would be flaky in CI.
Falsifiability, required by .sdlc/memory/conventions.md: raise `MAX_UNESCAPED_WILDCARDS` to 99 in a scratch edit, record the failing run showing 'bounds the pattern' going green-to-red, revert.

`unicodeLike('%%%%%%Z', 'Food')` returns 1 - a refused pattern is a match on the query side, keeping the axis from being narrower than the result set under `$like`. Under `$notlike` the compiler emits `(NOT UNICODE_LIKE(...) OR left IS NULL)`, so the same value yields no transactions, a strict subset of the axis.

The refusal is cached rather than recompiled: call `unicodeLike` twice with the same refused pattern and assert the LRU holds it. RUN THIS FILE WITH `yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test:node -- src/platform/server/sqlite/unicodeLike.test.ts`. It is collected by the NODE config, not the web one: `packages/loot-core/vitest.config.ts` excludes only `src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts` and `src/platform/server/fs/index.test.ts` and otherwise uses the default `**/*.test.ts` include, whereas `vitest.web.config.ts` sets `include:` to exactly those two files, so a CLI path argument against the web config matches nothing and runs zero tests. `package.json` `test` -> `npm-run-all -cp 'test:*'` -> `test:node`, so CI runs this file today. Do NOT pass `-t`: that hazard belongs to the two files that share process state via the sql.js wasm fetch, not to this file.
Pre-existing behaviour the cap must not change: `unicodeLike('%%%', 'Food')` and `unicodeLike('%?%', 'Food')` still return 1 - both 3-wildcard patterns, under the cap.
`unicodeLike(null, 'Food')` and `unicodeLike('', 'Food')` still return 0, so the line 11 early return is untouched by the retype.

In the 'reads text operators as LIKE patterns' describe (starts line 115), the AC-3 case for `contains`: `filterBy('contains', '%%%%%%Z')` equals `allIds` (all five wildcardCategories) - a refused pattern keeps every category rather than narrowing.

The paired `doesNotContain` case: `filterBy('doesNotContain', '%%%%%%Z')` ALSO equals `allIds`. The fail-closed trap and the single most important assertion in the change - if the axis empties here, money has left every total. Add a comment saying so. This unit assertion, not the browser step, carries IAC-3 directly.

The boundary case in the other direction: `filterBy('contains', '%%Z')` (4 wildcards, accepted) narrows exactly as the pattern says rather than keeping everything, so a fix that made every text condition a no-op fails here.

The grouped axis through `narrowCategoriesByConditions`, asserting CONTENTS AND NOT IDENTITY - the correction this plan makes after the last review. On a refused pattern the function does NOT return the input by identity: `filterCategoriesByConditions` reaches `categories.filter(...)` at budgetDataQuery.ts:291 and `Array.prototype.filter` always allocates, so the `list === categories.list` shortcut at line 151 does not fire and lines 155-167 rebuild. Assert: `expect(result).not.toBe(axis)`; `result.list.map(category => category.id)` equals the full axis id list; and `result.grouped.map(group => [group.id, (group.categories ?? []).map(c => c.id)])` equals the full `[['g-usual', ['c-food', 'c-rent']], ['g-bills', ['c-cell', 'c-net']]]`. Add a comment saying the identity shortcut covers only the three early returns (lines 176, 192, 202) and that contents-equal is what 'did not narrow' means here - which is exactly what IAC-3 asks for ('showing the axis still carries the full category set'). Use the existing `narrow()` helper at line 270 so the fixture is the one already in the file.
The paired `doesNotContain '%%%%%%Z'` case through the same helper, same contents assertion and the same `not.toBe(axis)`. If the axis empties here, money has left every total.

Pin the one real consequence of that rebuild so it is reviewable rather than surprising: an axis whose `grouped` contains a group with NO categories (add it to the fixture, or build one inline) has that group dropped under a refused pattern, because line 166 ends in `.filter(group => group.categories.length > 0)`. Assert the drop and say in a comment that it costs an empty row and never money, that `contains '%'` already behaves this way on unmodified main, and that this plan deliberately does NOT add an identity short-circuit for the refusal path.

The identity assertions that DO hold stay unchanged and are not edited: `narrowCategoriesByConditions(axis, [], 'or')` is `toBe(axis)` (line 452) and the uninterpretable-condition fallback (line 461) - both exercise the early returns, which is why they are unaffected by the refusal path.

Re-run the existing pinned cases unchanged and say so in the commit body: `contains '%'` and `contains '?'` keep every category, `contains '\\%'` narrows to `['c-discount']`, `contains 'o%'` narrows to three, `doesNotContain '%'` is `[]`, `matches 'x'.repeat(257)` keeps every category.
Falsifiability: invert the `doesNotContain` refusal to `matcher === null ? false : ...`, record the failing run, revert.

qa_script: Boot with `yarn start`, choose "Don't use a server", then click "Try the demo" (WelcomeScreen.tsx:130 - the button reads 'Try the demo', not 'View demo') for a populated budget. Note its size: 7 categories (Food, General, Bills, Bills (Flexible), Income, Starting Balances, Savings), far short of the several hundred IAC-1 names - see step 12.

Open Reports -> Custom report. Set the graph to 'Data Table' so rows are readable. Open the sidebar Options and turn ON 'Show empty rows' (ReportSidebar.tsx:493-494). It is OFF by default and every money assertion below depends on it being on. Note the full unfiltered category list - that is the reference set.

Add a filter: topbar Filters button -> field Category -> operator contains -> value `%%%%%%Z`. Assert the table renders promptly and the category list still shows every category from the reference set, with its real balance.

alternatives_considered.approach: Return a match-everything RegExp (`/^[\s\S]*$/i`) for a refused pattern instead of `null`, leaving both call sites untouched.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fails OPEN for `contains` and fails CLOSED for `doesNotContain`: that branch keeps a category when the regex does NOT match, so negating 'matches everything' drops every category - the axis becomes narrower than the query's result set and every category the query fetched loses its money from every total. The exact defect AC-3 exists to prevent, and it would have passed a `contains`-only test.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a `list.length === categories.list.length` short-circuit beside budgetDataQuery.ts:151 so the refusal path returns the axis BY IDENTITY, as the previous plan's tests[] asserted.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This was the alternative the last review offered and it is declined. (1) It is a behaviour change, not a bug fix: it changes what `contains '%'` and `contains '?'` do TODAY, since both already compile under the cap and already take the rebuild path - the two are indistinguishable from a refusal by length alone. The ticket's mandate is a bound on the compiler; changing the identity contract of the axis is a separate change that deserves its own ticket and its own review. (2) The identity the plan wanted is not what protects the money. The invariant that matters is that every kept category is still in the axis, and `list.length` equality is a weaker proxy for that than contents equality: a future filter that dropped and re-added nothing would satisfy it while a group whose members changed would not. (3) The tests[] assertion it enabled was the false claim the review caught, so the choice is to assert the true contract instead. The rebuild's one real effect - dropping an already-empty input group, which holds no money - is pinned by a test rather than designed away.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep AC-3's browser assertion with 'Show empty rows' at its default (off), on the reasoning that an empty doesNotContain report is the tell.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is not a tell. With showEmpty false, `filterEmptyRows` (filterEmptyRows.ts:24) drops every zero-balance row, so the query's empty result set renders an empty table on a correct implementation too - the two are the same picture. The only browser setting that separates them is showEmpty true, where correct shows the full axis at 0.00 and fail-closed shows nothing. This is what the previous review objected to and it is right.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep `likePatternToRegex` total and add a sibling `isPatternWithinBounds(pattern)` that consumers must remember to call.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves the unbounded compile reachable - a caller that forgets the check gets the catastrophic regex with nothing to stop it, which is the hazard the ticket names when it says the bound must live inside the function. It also splits one definition of the pattern language across two exports in the file that declares itself the single definition.

alternatives_considered.approach: Throw from `likePatternToRegex` on a refused pattern and let each caller catch.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `unicodeLike` is a sqlite scalar function invoked per row from inside the query engine; an exception there escapes as a raw engine error rather than a fail-open result, and a per-row try/catch is the wrong shape for a control-flow signal on the hottest path in the file.

alternatives_considered.approach: Bound the value at the report UI - strip or reject wildcard characters in the Category filter field.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes one entry point and leaves every other one unbounded: transaction rules reach the same `$like` path through `transaction-rules.ts`, and so does `forecast-filters.ts`. It also cannot satisfy AC-2, which requires the bound to live in the shared function.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the hang by memoising `likePatternToRegex` in the report axis.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The measurement says so and I reproduced it on this runner: compilation was <=0.09 ms for every pattern, including the 7-wildcard one that takes 15.6 s to test. Caching the regex would remove a fraction of a percent of the cost. The bound is the fix.

alternatives_considered.approach: Give `canNarrowAxisByConditions` a direct test instead of unexporting it (the other branch AC-6 allows).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: All four branches are already covered through `narrowCategoriesByConditions`, its only caller and only observable contract (budgetDataQuery.test.ts lines 403, 416, 436, 452). A second table asserting the same four outcomes through a private function is exactly the kind of test that drifts from the first, and it would keep a gate with no independent meaning exported for a future caller to depend on. The reason is recorded next to the function, as AC-6 requires.

alternatives_considered.approach: Carry IAC-3 entirely as a unit assertion and drop its browser half.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves the ticket's second surface - what a person sees in the report - unverified in the product, and the unit test cannot reach `filterEmptyRows`, the one place where a correct axis is turned back into an empty screen. The two halves together make the fail-closed direction non-vacuous, so the browser half is kept - with the toggle on.

assumptions: The wildcard count, not the pattern length, is what bounds the cost. Confirmed by measurement: a 6-character value producing an 8-wildcard pattern is where AC-1's hang lives, and no length cap below ~6 would touch it.

4 is the right cap. It keeps the accepted region at ~46 ms across 300 categories (measured here), admits every value the existing pinned tests exercise (`%` and `?` compile to 3-wildcard patterns, verified by running the compiler), and admits any realistic user input - no plausible category filter contains three or more unescaped wildcards.

Treating a refusal as a match on the query side (`unicodeLike` -> 1) is the correct pairing with an axis that keeps every category, because it makes the query's result set a subset of the axis in both operator directions. The alternative pairing (refusal -> 0) also satisfies the subset invariant, so the choice is made on least surprise: `contains` returns everything and `doesNotContain` returns nothing, rather than the reverse.
`isSupportedCategoryCondition` already guarantees `typeof condition.value === 'string'` for `contains` and `doesNotContain`, so the new non-string guards are defensive and do not change behaviour.

The report axis runs synchronously in the React component body (custom-spreadsheet.ts:93, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:45), which is why the freeze is on the main thread and why the bound is worth having on this path even though the query-side UNICODE_LIKE runs elsewhere.

QA can reach 'Show empty rows' in the Custom report's sidebar Options popover in the running app. The control is wired at ReportSidebar.tsx:493-494 (`name: 'show-empty-items'`, text 'Show empty rows') and its handler sets `showEmpty` on both the session report and the passed setter; if it is disabled for some configuration QA uses, AC-10's unit assertions carry IAC-3 directly.

The empty-input-group case in the new test can be built from the existing `makeAxis()` fixture in budgetDataQuery.test.ts:270 without restructuring the file - the fixture is local to the `narrowCategoriesByConditions` describe and this change adds no shared helper.

The demo budget has 7 categories and an 8-wildcard pattern against 7 names costs a few milliseconds, so the pre-fix multi-minute hang is not reproducible there. AC-1 is written to what a live browser can see and AC-8 carries the falsifiable form of the same claim; if QA can reach a budget with several hundred categories, the timing is worth measuring and recording in the PR.

Whether any consumer outside this repository imports `REGEX_SPECIAL`. The package's `exports` map exposes `./shared/*` as a direct file path, so the name was reachable; a repo-wide grep across packages/ and scripts/ found no reference outside its own module, and this package is not published for third-party consumption as `@actual-app/core` in any configuration I could see.

validated_work_order.debate_summary:
The last review raised one objection against version 2, and it is correct; this version is built around answering it directly.

Objection: tests[] told the implementer to assert that `narrowCategoriesByConditions` returns the input BY IDENTITY (`toBe(axis)`) for `contains '%%%%%%Z'` and `doesNotContain '%%%%%%Z'`, calling that 'the existing contract for did not narrow'. A refused pattern keeps every category, but `filterCategoriesByConditions` returns a fresh array. The required choice was (a) drop the identity assertion and state what the function actually returns, or (b) make identity on a refusal a stated behaviour change with its own acceptance criterion.

Confirmed against source before choosing: budgetDataQuery.ts:291 is `return categories.filter(cat => ...)`, `Array.prototype.filter` always allocates, the `list === categories.list` shortcut at line 151 is therefore false on the refusal path, and lines 155-167 rebuild. Only the early returns at lines 176, 192 and 202 return the input by identity, none reachable by a supported `contains` condition. The plan's own reading of the same file contradicted it: the identity assertions it cited (lines 452, 461) exercise only those early returns.

CHOSEN: (a). What the function actually returns for a refused pattern is a NEW object whose `list` is a new array of the same category entities in the same order, and whose `grouped` is a new array of new group objects each holding all of its members - with the one further consequence that line 166's `.filter(group => group.categories.length > 0)` drops a group that was ALREADY EMPTY in the input. That costs an empty row and never money, and it is not a regression: `contains '%'` already takes the same rebuild path on unmodified main.

APPLIED THROUGHOUT, not just to the flagged sentence. (1) tests[] for budgetDataQuery.test.ts: the identity case is replaced by a contents assertion for both operators - full id list, full group/category map, plus `expect(result).not.toBe(axis)` so the test proves the rebuild happened rather than passing by accident - and a new case pins the already-empty-group drop. The reviewer noted the doesNotContain sentence repeated the same claim; both are rewritten. (2) AC-10 is new: IAC-3's 'showing the axis still carries the full category set' as a tested contract, with contents equality rather than identity as the check. (3) `approach` states the refusal path's real return shape and the empty-group consequence in full, so the implementer does not re-derive it. (4) files[] edit (4) is new: the doc comment at lines 115-125 ('When no condition narrows anything, the input is returned unchanged by identity') and the one at lines 148-150 ('returns its input untouched whenever it cannot safely narrow') both become false the moment a refusal exists, and per .sdlc/memory/conventions.md a comment that misdescribes the code above it is a defect this repo has merged PRs over - see .sdlc/memory/patterns/planner-read-comment-wording-as-the-defect.md, which records nine PRs re-litigating comment wording and test strength. Fixing them here costs nothing, since this change is already editing both call sites in the same function.

Option (b) is recorded as a considered alternative with its reasons rather than dismissed: making identity on a refusal a behaviour change would alter what `contains '%'` does today (it is under the cap and already rebuilds), which is a different change from the compiler bound the ticket asks for; and `list.length` equality is a weaker proxy for the money invariant than contents equality. If a person wants it, it should be its own ticket - named in out_of_scope so the implementer does not wander into it.

Nothing else from the previous rejection changed. The bound still lives in `likePatternToRegex` and still returns `null`; it still fails open on both operators; the cap is still 4; AC-3 still runs with 'Show empty rows' enabled; AC-2 still hands over the `test:node` command that actually collects the file. The cost curve behind the cap was re-measured on this runner (4/5/6/7 wildcards -> 46 ms / 375 ms / 2465 ms / 15555 ms across 300 categories, compile <=0.09 ms throughout), which independently reproduces the previous plan's shape rather than inheriting it.
residual_risks: If a future report grows a third LIKE consumer, the type change forces it to handle the refusal, but nothing forces it to handle it in the OPEN direction. The invariant is written into the module doc comment and asserted on both operators (AC-10), so the next review has something to check against.

AC-3's browser half depends on QA performing the 'Show empty rows' step. The toggle is now step 2 of the qa_script and named in the criterion's how_to_verify, but a QA run that skips it will see an empty doesNotContain report on a correct build. That is why the paired unit assertions are required rather than optional: IAC-3 is carried by the tests even if the browser half is skipped.

The refusal path's rebuild is asserted as contents-equality rather than identity. If a future change alters `filterCategoriesByConditions` so a keep-everything result again returns its input untouched, the new tests keep passing (they assert contents, plus `not.toBe(axis)` which would then fail) - which is the intended looseness: the tests pin the money invariant, and `not.toBe(axis)` pins the rebuild as a fact about this implementation rather than as the contract. If the shortcut is ever made unconditional, that one assertion is what will need updating, and it is named as a consequence in the test comment.

No test was executed while writing this plan - the checkout has no node_modules. The test-collection claims come from reading the two vitest configs, and the cost curve from a standalone script that reproduces `likePatternToRegex` verbatim. The implementer's first action should be `yarn install` and a full `yarn test` to confirm the existing suite is green before the change, since a pre-existing failure would otherwise be misread as caused by it.
